PullRequest.Title: sessions: add environment grouping to the sessions list
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Adds **Environment** alongside Time, Workspace, and Repository in the Agents window's sessions-list grouping controls.

- Groups sessions across agents and workspaces under This Computer, Cloud, or their remote host using provider-neutral, stable environment identities.
- Matches Workspace/Repository behavior for section reordering, Recent/All capping, filtering, comparison-group placement, and New Session actions.
- Includes desktop and mobile controls, environment-specific Show More labels and ARIA text, workspace badges, accessibility help, documentation, and regression tests.
- Preserves pinned, archived, explicit custom-group, external-session, and quick-chat placement precedence; disconnected and unknown hosts do not lose their sessions.

## Stack

First of two feature PRs; merge this one first. The follow-up, #343239, adds nesting workspace, repository, and environment sections inside custom groups and targets this branch.

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window with sessions from This Computer, Cloud, and/or remote hosts.
2. In Filter Sessions > Grouping, select Environment. Verify sessions from different agents and workspaces share the appropriate environment section and retain workspace badges.
3. Exercise Recent/All, Show More/Show Less, environment filtering, section reordering, New Session, and pinned/archived sessions.
4. On phone layout, use Sort and select Group by Environment.

## Validation

- `git diff --check 386203d9b1559d29e9bab2ce9a19800230d13cc6..16266fd5eab` — passed.
- Isolated environment-only snapshot — TypeScript syntax checks and internal dependency bundling passed for the sessions-list, view-menu, and view-pane test entry points. External packages were excluded; these are not executed unit tests or a TypeScript type check.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — blocked: missing root `node_modules/gulp/bin/gulp.js`. Earlier dependency restoration with `npm run install-fast` failed with registry authentication `E401`.
- Full unit tests, ESLint, TypeScript type checking, and live UI validation were not completed because the required dependencies are unavailable.
- Focused suite to run once dependencies are restored: `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewMenu.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewPane.test.ts` — not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select Environment grouping and render or refresh the Sessions list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit grouping choice persists one profile value, then synchronously filters and sorts sessions, normalizes the in-memory provider environment catalogue, groups sessions by environment, applies section/session caps, and calls tree.setChildren before the new list is visible. Later observable session changes are coalesced to the next animation frame where applicable; provider/filter changes call the same update directly.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected grouping value in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one storage write per explicit grouping change, independent of session count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selecting Workspace, Repository, or Time already performed the same single profile-storage write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write occurs before the synchronous list update, but it is the existing persistence path used by every grouping mode.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N filtered sessions, P registered providers/environments, and C comparison groups. The new environment path adds O(P log P) normalization and O(N) grouping plus a sort over distinct environments; the pre-existing update already sorts sessions and builds O(N) list state. Default capping limits rendered session rows per environment section.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI-thread work is serialized. Session/chat observable refreshes use a single next-animation-frame slot, while direct provider/filter changes run one update per event; no parallel boundary calls are launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider and session data are already resident in memory. Environment normalization is recomputed per update rather than cached, but P is the small registered-provider catalogue; there is no cold I/O or network miss path. Section/session caps and persisted expansion state behave the same on cold and warm renders.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and cardinalities from SessionsView.setGrouping, SessionsList.update, SessionsProvidersService.getProviders, getSessionEnvironments, and groupByEnvironment.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations can retain many sessions, but the added work is linear in those already traversed by the existing list rebuild and provider cardinality is normally small. No evidence shows a newly dominant cost or dropped-frame mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the feature adds bounded in-memory grouping comparable to existing workspace/repository grouping and introduces no per-session expensive boundary or eager uncapped DOM rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand Show More, switch Recent/All, or use Find while grouped by Environment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The interaction updates presentation state and rebuilds the object tree. Recent mode limits sessions within each environment and hides non-primary environment sections; Show More or active Find intentionally creates tree elements for the requested additional sessions before tree reconciliation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The default path renders at most the configured per-section session limit plus primary environment sections. Explicit Show All/Find scales with matching sessions and nested chats, exactly as existing workspace/repository modes do.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread rebuild; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls were found on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Expansion/capping choices are read from profile-backed in-memory state during rendering. Tree virtualization/reconciliation is reused; there is no new cache key or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from renderSessionChildren, limitSessionsForList, partitioning, and tree.setChildren call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large explicit Show All results can still create substantial object-tree state, but that behavior and total-session cardinality predate this mode; environment grouping does not increase the total number of session/chat elements.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: default rendering remains capped, and uncapped work occurs only under the same explicit controls already available in other section grouping modes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a new session from an Environment section
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On an explicit toolbar click, getNewSessionSources scans that section's sessions and performs in-memory provider lookups to select the newest available source, then opens one composer and applies one workspace/provider selection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(S) over sessions in the selected environment section, deduplicated to one source per environment; because an Environment section has one environment, the action resolves one source and never fans out by session or workspace.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited new-session UI transition followed by one synchronous workspace selection; no loop starts providers, IPC calls, subprocesses, filesystem operations, or network requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider availability comes from the resident provider registry; no cache misses or retries are introduced. Disconnected providers are skipped during the scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from NewSessionForWorkspaceAction.run, getNewSessionSources, openNewSessionLike, and SessionsService._openNewSession.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: An environment section may contain many retained sessions, but this scan is user-triggered once per New Session click and performs constant-cost in-memory lookups.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the changed action performs one linear in-memory selection and one creation workflow, rather than per-session boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reorder Environment sections among custom groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A drag computes the existing visible top-level order, merges the moved environment identity into the persisted order, serializes the small order/promoted state, and triggers one list update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the serialized section-order and promotion state in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage write for a successful drag; no writes while hovering or for no-op drops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Workspace/repository section and custom-group drops already merged and persisted the same order state once per successful drop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write occurs in the explicit drop handler before the resulting update event; this is the same path used by workspace and repository section reordering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible top-level groups plus distinct environment sections. Environment identities add only one entry per environment, and stale entries are removed by retain when sessions/groups disappear.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized user interaction on the UI thread with one storage operation and one emitted update; no concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Order and promotion state are held in memory after startup and persisted after mutations. The new environment identities participate in the existing lifecycle cleanup, so they do not create unbounded retained keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from moveHeader, SessionSectionOrderService.reorder/save, and liveSectionOrderIds/retain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact count of remote hosts varies, but it is bounded by live session environments and is typically much smaller than session count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new identities reuse a bounded, cleaned-up persistence path with unchanged write cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and relevant callers. The new mode adds bounded in-memory environment normalization/grouping and reuses existing capping, tree reconciliation, storage, and action paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced latency, fan-out, retention, rendering, or concurrency regression was found.
